newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook- Gas oil testing new support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook- Gas oil testing new support.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil market was facing a break of $24.00-per-barrel support this week as a supply glut faced weak regional demand, traders said on Monday.
Prompt physical gas oil has not traded below $24.00 since July last year.

Traders said the market would remain soft in July and was projected to pick up moderately only in August when buyers were expected to emerge ahead of winter and when Indonesia is xpected to buy to cover for refinery shutdowns.
This would pressure the contango to widen from its current 60 cents per barrel between mid-June and early July, they said.
But some traders noted that the recovery could be moderated by the return of the bulk of South Korean refineries from annual maintenance shutdowns during August and September.
They said South Korean refiners have been active sellers in Asia this year and were fast carving a niche in China. For example in April, they sold 25 cargoes to the mainland.

To illustrate present China's lack of interest, traders said South Korean sellers were now offering gas oil into southern China at 40 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis, but was still receiving a cool response from Chinese buyers.
Amid high stocks in Hong Kong, premiums have slid below 70 cents per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f basis, compared to more than $1.00 premium over a month ago.

The current situation was worsened by an open arbitrage from the Mediterranean with four cargoes heading to Asia and with more expected to be fixed. Asia sellers were also facing stiff competition from Middle Eastern refineries.
The current spread between the Mediterranean and Asia was assessed at $27.00 per tonne, traders said.

Traders said that at current rate, gas oil values might fall below jet fuel. But the outlook for jet fuel was also gloomy amid poor regional demand and India taking only one kerosene cargo for July delivery.

The gasoline market was also bearish as Taiwan bought one cargo of 95-octane unleaded for second-half July delivery at $24.70 per barrel, c-and-f basis. This was between 22 and 50 cents below the last two cargoes that Taiwan purchased for end-June and early July deliveries.
But gasoline values were expected to recover in the medium term amid limited South Korean and Chinese exports while refinery shutdowns in Indonesia could spur imports.
The spot naphtha market was at a standstill as buyers focused on term talks.

The market was also weighed down by abundant arbitrage cargoes from the Mediterranean, but a recovery was expected in August when North Asian petrochemical plants are due to return from maintenance turnarounds, traders said.
Traders said the MidEast naphtha market might be under pressure with Saudi Aramco offering additional cargoes of A-180 between June and September.
The high sulphur fuel oil market was expected to hover above $100 per tonne this week but sentiment was slightly weak in the absence of fresh buying support, traders said.
Although summer supplies are tight, at least five cargoes are heading East from the Mediterranean and the Middle East for mid-June arrival, they said.
No cargo was traded last week with the market consolidating around $101/$102 per tonne, fob basis, against its last traded level of $101.50.
The market was also awaiting results for two tenders from Taiwan and India this week.
